modelGuidance:
Luna is the lowest-cost, fastest workflow model. Use it for token-intensive gathering, filtering, and organizing evidence, including browser interaction, web research, session-history retrieval, broad inventories, and extracting facts from many files or records. Luna should report evidence, source locations, and coverage gaps rather than make consequential technical decisions from incomplete evidence. It is the only workflow model allowed to use browser tools. Fable or Opus should direct investigations requiring engineering judgment and interpret Luna's findings.

Fable is the planner for architectural changes, ambiguous or conflicting requirements, and changes spanning multiple areas where existing patterns do not settle the design. Have it map domain rules, evaluate tradeoffs, and define actionable implementation steps and edge-case scenarios. Scope and design complexity, not file count alone, determine whether planning is needed. Do not make a Fable plan a mandatory step for routine changes.

Opus is the default implementation model for delegated coding. Give it the requirements and any agreed design, have it implement the change, run relevant builds and tests, and report residual risks. It can investigate and implement directly when a separate architecture plan is unnecessary. Use medium for routine implementation and high for consequential or complex domain changes.

Astra is the independent reviewer and validator when behavioral or architectural risk justifies a second perspective. Give it the requirements, baseline, and resulting plan or diff; have it challenge assumptions, accounting and edge-case behavior, compatibility, and verification. Prefer an independent review over merely endorsing the implementer's self-assessment. Do not invoke every model by default or add agents solely to increase count.
